analysis: Only CHANGELOG.md was changed; no executable source or threat-model text is visible, so the findings are threat-model gaps rather than code regressions. The changelog entries consistent with the existing model include the SEC-035 re-acceptance of the 30-minute SSD TTL (line 598), removal of caller top-level user, metadata, safety_identifier and prompt_cache_key from provider-bound bodies (line 281), removal of the unauthenticated earnings endpoint (T-031, line 573), fail-closed attestation challenges (line 575), App Attest protocol 3 only (line 577), and the frozen legacy MDM cohort with the /v1/enroll proof requirement (lines 301-310, with direct MicroMDM enrollment of copied profiles documented). New surfaces flagged: coordinator-persisted cache routing state (475-479), the referral rewards program (230-235), and Resend provider emails (221). The next pass should check the actual code for each: cache persistence keyed only by the server-HMAC scope and deleted on erasure, reward settlement idempotency and chargeback handling, and email export authorization.

findings.detail: The changelog says SSD cache holders and observed demand are now written behind to the coordinator database and restored after restart. T-041 only models provider-side SSD artifacts and the in-process TTFT oracle, and treats the coordinator's cacheSalt scoping as the isolation control. A new durable coordinator store holding account-scoped routing evidence has two consequences the model does not address. Reuse and the same-account timing oracle can persist across coordinator restarts, and a restored row could be bound to the wrong scope or provider if the keyed scope or capability check regresses. T-059 account erasure also does not obviously cover these rows. Update T-041 and T-059 to cover the persisted rows, their TTL and cutoff, and their deletion on erasure and account scope change, and verify that rows are keyed only by the server-HMAC scope.
findings.title: Coordinator-side durable cache-holder persistence is not covered by the cache or erasure threat entries

findings.detail: The Open Sales Program pays referrers 5% of referred consumers' collected spend as withdrawable earnings funded by Darkbloom, with referral codes and attribution recorded per account. TB-008 and T-060 cover the ledger and reward administration but not consumer-driven reward farming. The changelog excludes self-routing and selected-machine routing, but it does not mention a defense against sybil accounts, wash spend that is refunded or charged back, or a referrer who also controls the serving provider. Withdrawable credit funded by the platform is a direct cash-out path. Add a threat entry covering these cases, with mitigations such as chargeback or refund clawback, a payout hold, and detection of linked accounts or providers.
findings.title: Referral reward program adds a payment-abuse surface that is absent from the threat model

findings.detail: The `provider-emails` command syncs provider owner email addresses and groups to Resend and creates broadcasts. This is a new third-party PII flow. T-059 models account-erasure leftovers but does not cover external mailing-list copies, and the broadcast tooling is an operator-credentialed surface that could expose owner-to-machine associations. The changelog says unsubscribe preferences are preserved and owners are removed from groups once their machines meet the target. It does not say that account erasure deletes the Resend contact. Document the flow and make erasure remove the contact from Resend.
findings.title: Provider owner emails are synced to a third party (Resend) without a modeled data flow or erasure path
